title: Climate-linked migration is forcing health systems to treat mobility, displacement, and resilience as one connected policy problem
source_unit: World Health Organization, Global research prioritization and action plan on health, migration and displacement in the context of climate change, 2026
geography: Global migration, displacement, climate, and health systems across origin, transit, destination, and return contexts

observations.period: 2026; climate, mobility, and health-system research agenda

denominator.unit: WHO Global Research Prioritization Exercise on health, migration, displacement, and climate change

linked_driver.value: climate change is treated both as an increasingly important driver of migration and displacement and as a determinant of health

journey_scope.value: health risks and access barriers must be studied across the migration journey rather than only at a destination point

core_themes.value: priority research is organized around social determinants of health, universal health coverage, and emergencies

boundary.value: the report prioritizes evidence gaps and action; it is not a prevalence estimate or causal evaluation of climate migration health effects

observations.method: WHO structured and participatory research-prioritization exercise using a scoping review, technical consultations, and stakeholder surveys.
observations.uncertainty: Research priorities identify important unknowns and coordination needs but do not quantify the magnitude or direction of every health pathway.
observations.subgroup: Migrants, refugees, internally displaced people, people in transit, host communities, health workers, and populations exposed to climate hazards.
observations.counterinterpretation: Migration can also reduce exposure to climate hazards or improve access to care, depending on legal status, resources, route, and receiving-system capacity.

denominator.unit: WHO identified evidence-gap cluster on migrant and displaced populations

determinants.value: the agenda prioritizes effects of social and structural determinants on health across migration and displacement contexts

access.value: barriers to health-care access and inclusion in health systems are identified as major gaps

intersectionality.value: the report calls for improved data and intersectional analyses to distinguish how legal status, gender, age, disability, poverty, race, place, and climate exposure combine

analytic_signal.value: mobility status is not a sufficient explanation: health outcomes depend on the interaction of material conditions, rights, services, social position, and environmental exposure

observations.method: WHO synthesis of scoping evidence, stakeholder input, and technical prioritization across social determinants and universal health coverage.
observations.uncertainty: The prioritization does not supply harmonized subgroup estimates or establish that any single determinant dominates across settings.
observations.subgroup: People with insecure legal status, women and girls, children, older people, people with disabilities, low-income households, and marginalized ethnic or racial groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad intersectional categories can improve visibility while still requiring local data, participatory interpretation, and safeguards against stereotyping.

denominator.unit: WHO action-plan route for migration, displacement, climate, and health emergencies

emergency_inclusion.value: inclusion of migrants and displaced populations in emergency responses is a named evidence gap and action priority

long_term.value: long-term health impacts of displacement require research beyond immediate crisis response

resilience.value: the proposed roadmap calls for equitable, climate-resilient health responses coordinated across sectors

analytic_signal.value: health-system resilience is partly a portability and continuity problem: care, data, protection, and emergency support must travel across changing places and statuses

observations.method: WHO action-plan and roadmap synthesis linking research priorities to policy and practice.
observations.uncertainty: A roadmap establishes a coordination direction, not evidence that health systems can currently sustain continuity across borders or displacement episodes.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people, migrants in transit, host health systems, emergency responders, community organizations, and cross-border public authorities.
observations.counterinterpretation: National health systems may have stronger continuity than cross-border data suggests, while centralized coordination may overlook local or community-led care networks.

denominator.unit: WHO cross-cutting research themes: data, policy and interventions; health outcomes

cross_cutting.value: data, policy and interventions, and health outcomes are treated as cross-cutting themes rather than separate silos

knowledge_gap.value: the report emphasizes improved data, coordinated interdisciplinary research, and translation into policy and practice

governance_route.value: evidence quality depends on collaboration across health, migration, climate, emergency, social-protection, and other sectors

open_test.value: join climate hazard, movement or immobility, legal status, housing and work conditions, service access, continuity, health outcome, and later institutional response without treating aggregate priorities as individual histories

observations.method: WHO Global Research Prioritization Exercise and proposed joint action plan.
observations.uncertainty: The agenda identifies priority questions but does not guarantee comparable data, funding, implementation, or causal inference across countries.
observations.subgroup: Researchers, public-health agencies, migration authorities, humanitarian actors, climate planners, civil society, and affected communities.
observations.counterinterpretation: More data and coordination can improve policy while also creating privacy, surveillance, consent, and cross-border data-governance risks.

related_sources.claim: The official WHO page provides the report date, methodology, core themes, cross-cutting themes, and action-plan framing.
The report's downloadable publication is the primary source for the research-prioritization exercise and roadmap.
WHO South-East Asia UHC monitoring supplies a complementary regional service and climate-health monitoring route.

boundary: This record adds a climate-mobility-health route from social and structural exposure through health-care access, emergency inclusion, continuity, data infrastructure, and climate-resilient public response. It is a WHO research-prioritization agenda, not respondent-level data, a prevalence estimate, a causal evaluation, or proof that climate change produces one uniform migration or health outcome.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official WHO publication page was reviewed for the climate-migration-health framing, migration-journey scope, three core themes, two cross-cutting themes, evidence gaps, participatory method, and action-plan route.
